mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances where GDPC1 YoY growth accelerates by > 1pp.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises by more than 0.5 percentage points over 3 months, it signals a weakening labor market and potential economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that will slow economic growth and produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 40% of periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment growth slows by more than 100,000 jobs per month for two consecutive months, it signals a weakening labor market and potential recession, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth slows by > 100k jobs/mo for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts decline by more than 10% year-over-year, it signals a weakening housing market and consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production growth accelerates by more than 1% month-over-month, it signals a strengthening economy and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of instances where INDPRO growth accelerates by > 1% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate and the unemployment rate both rise by more than 0.5 percentage points over 3 months, it signals a tightening monetary policy and a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and UNRATE both rise > 0.5pp in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP growth and retail sales both decline by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter, it signals a weakening consumer demand environment and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and RSAFS both decline > 1% QoQ
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances.
